# Vendored packages

Packages the web client installs by path (`web/package.json`, `file:vendor/...`).

## nib-core-0.10.0.tgz

`@nib/core` 0.10.0, nib's framework-free editor core and its chrome. The Nodes stage (`web/src/NibEditor.tsx`)
mounts its `Editor` with `mountEditor` on the selected revision's `map.json` and nib's chrome over it with
`mountChrome(container, editor, { actions: ['save'] })`, styled by `@nib/core/chrome.css`; the chrome's Save posts
the map nib wrote to `POST /api/revisions/{revision_id}/map`, which makes a new trace revision. The package depends on
`lucide` (the chrome's icon data), which `npm` installs with it. It reads and writes the planar map's setting in either form t3api writes: the per-kind half-width table (`{half, A1, A2, L}`, t3api 0.27.0, ending with the optional `min_sweep: {arc, ellipse}` from 0.29.0) and the older `{w, A1, A2, L}` (up to 0.26.0), each written back byte for byte, so the Nodes stage opens maps traced with either. It has Retract handles (Shift+H, the chrome button "Retract handles (Shift+H)", Ctrl+click on one handle), a tap on a face that makes its label's layer active and marks its row in the layers panel, and draws a face whose ring is one piece closing on itself (with the hole it cuts in the face around it). Hiding a face gives its area to its visible neighbour with the longest shared boundary (the taker's fill covers it, so a hidden face leaves no hole); Merge face (Delete on a face row, or Del with every node of one face selected) merges a face into that neighbour as one undoable edit; the panel's delete button on a label map merges a face row and is disabled, with a title saying why, on a layer row; and a closed ring of one node takes an inserted node and a reshaped segment. 0.7.1 makes every chrome icon a lucide icon: the layers panel's header buttons (Add layer, Add group, the isolate toggle, delete, Collapse panel), its collapsed tab and a group row's expand / collapse chevron, as its hide, lock and active buttons already were. 0.8.0 reads, validates and writes back t3api 0.29.0's arc minimum sweep in the setting (`min_sweep`, absent at the default), so a map traced at a minimum sweep opens and saves byte for byte. 0.9.0 adds the boundary tool on a label map (B, the toolbar's "Draw a boundary" and the help sheet's B line): a Bezier pen that draws dashed drafts split at every crossing, and a tap in a face that opens the label picker and commits the drafts bounding that face as edges with its new label, or relabels a whole face, in one command that undoes byte for byte. Its `checkLabelMap` also enforces the rule of the map: no edge has one label on both sides. 0.9.1 makes a picked colour equal to a palette entry that entry: the picker shows its swatch as chosen and the commit takes its label, so the palette never holds one colour twice. 0.9.2 removes a retracted handle instead of leaving it at zero length: a handle on its own node's point is no handle, so after Shift+H none is drawn at the node, a press there takes and drags the node, and H grows the handle back. 0.9.3 deletes a label map's node by what it is (Del, one command "Delete node"): a ring's own node goes and the ring keeps its shape less that node; deleting the node of a one-piece ring removes the ring, and its face merges into the face around it; a node where two edges meet joins them; a junction or a canvas-border node is refused with a notice naming how many nodes stayed and why, and the selection stays on them. In an SVG document, deleting a path's last node deletes the path. 0.9.4 makes Merge face keep the rule of the map: when the merged face's neighbour comes to touch another face of its own label, that face merges in too, in the same one undoable edit, so no edge is left with one label on both sides. 0.9.5 keeps a save point in the undo history: a label-map save the host reports saved keeps the editor's history, and `EditorStats.unsaved` says whether the map differs from its last save, so the Nodes stage keeps its editor as it is across a save. 0.10.0 adds the Add node tool (the toolbar's "Add node", a one shot that snaps as the boundary tool does and inserts one node) and the symmetric node letter `z` in label maps (cusp, smooth and symmetric cycle; a node with a straight side passes over symmetric); keeps a smooth node a tangent join through every edit; inserts a double-clicked or touch double-tapped node at the exact nearest point of the segment, with a touch reach of max(8, half the contact size, 22) CSS px; scrolls the paths panel to a path selected on the canvas; keeps the boundary tool working after a pick, merge, undo or redo changes the map under it, its frame loop surviving an error; keeps the shape when a node is deleted; and draws the drafts, draft-node squares and face hatch two-tone, so a new boundary shows on a black face.

## Replacing it with a new pack

1. In nib, check out the tag to ship (`git -C <nib> describe --tags` names it) and run `pnpm pack
   --pack-destination <vinylgen>/web/vendor` in `packages/core`.
2. Delete the old tarball from this folder. If the version changed, change the `file:` path in
   `web/package.json` to the new file name.
3. Update this README: file name, sha256 (`sha256sum`), version, tag and commit.
4. Run `npm --prefix web install` so `web/package-lock.json` records the new tarball's integrity, then
   `just test` and `npm --prefix web run build`. `just deploy` runs `npm --prefix web ci`, which installs the
   tarball the lockfile records.
